title: StrategyActivated.v1
description: A strategy version became ACTIVE and is now deciding (A§23, A§60). Emitted by strategy-service on `collections.strategy` keyed by `strategyId`, in the same transaction as the activation, which atomically retires the previously ACTIVE version — so an activation always appears as this event plus a `StrategyRetired` for the version it replaced, never one without the other. decision-service consumes it to refresh its configuration cache (with a 60s poll as a fallback, so a missed event delays a strategy by a minute rather than stranding it). Activation must be auditable (A§60): the append-only `strategy_transition` row is the record, this event is the notification.

strategyId.description: Identifier of the strategy family that was activated, e.g. `EARLY_COLLECTION`. Also the partition key of the event, so activations and retirements of one strategy are strictly ordered.

version.description: Version of the strategy that is now ACTIVE. At most one version of a strategy is ACTIVE at a time, enforced in the database by a partial unique index (DEC-2), not merely by application logic.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the canonical JSON of the activated `strategy-document.v1.json`. Frozen at the TEST→SIMULATED transition and unchanged through the approvals, so a consumer — or an auditor years later — can prove that what was approved is what went live. A definition edit changes the hash and invalidates the simulation and the approvals.

effectiveFrom.description: First business date (UTC calendar date) on which this version decides, copied from the activated definition. Activation may happen before this date — SCHEDULED then ACTIVE — so a consumer must honour the date rather than assume "active now means deciding now".

activatedBy.description: Who activated it: the identity provider `sub` of the human who pressed activate, or `system:strategy-scheduler` when the scheduler tick promoted a SCHEDULED version on its effective date. Never a display name — the audit needs a stable identifier.
